rationale: Sharpened the precondition of the snapshot-boundary loop and corrected an over-general reading. The three-case harness now runs the same legal five-node history with (TrailingLogs=0, no post-snapshot entries), (TrailingLogs=10, 20 post-snapshot entries) and (TrailingLogs=25, 20 post-snapshot entries). Only the first loops; in both nonzero cases the leader's snapshot at index 4 compacts nothing because at snapshot time its log had not yet extended TrailingLogs past the snapshot index, so the leader could still walk the prev-log index down and the peer converged. The loop therefore requires lastLog - snapshotIndex >= TrailingLogs at the moment of snapshotting, not merely 'some compaction'.

investigations.question: At the moment a leader takes the snapshot that a rejoining follower needs, must the leader's log already extend TrailingLogs entries past the snapshot index for the boundary to be compacted away, and does the loop disappear whenever it does not?

knowledge.statement: compactLogsWithTrailing returns without deleting anything when lastLogIdx <= trailingLogs, and otherwise deletes up to maxLog = min(snapshotIndex, lastLogIdx - trailingLogs). A snapshot is taken at the FSM's applied index, so in a quiet cluster snapshotIndex is close to lastLogIdx and the deletion stops well below the snapshot index, leaving the leader able to serve entries below its snapshot boundary. The leader's retained first index passes the snapshot index only when lastLogIdx - trailingLogs >= snapshotIndex at snapshot time, i.e. when the log end is at least TrailingLogs ahead of the snapshot index when the snapshot is taken. TrailingLogs=0 satisfies this by construction.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to any LogStore with a trailing-log configuration; the arithmetic is in compactLogsWithTrailing, and the snapshot index is the FSM's applied index at the time of the snapshot (user-triggered or threshold-triggered).

interpretations.rationale: Local construction feedback from the three-case harness (non-retained; the experiment is registered for the controller to execute). Case (TrailingLogs=0, post=0): successor_snapshot at index 4 with store 0/0 and rejoin_observe restores_early 723 / restores_late 733, partner_applied_index 4, partner_last_index 7 - the loop. Case (TrailingLogs=10, post=20): the same snapshot at index 4 leaves the successor's store at 1..24 (store_first 1), i.e. nothing was compacted at the boundary, and rejoin_observe reports restores_before/early/late all 0 with partner_applied_index 24 and partner_last_index 24 - full convergence. Case (TrailingLogs=25, post=20): identical shape, store 1..24, restores 0, partner applied and last index 24. The discriminating arithmetic is compactLogsWithTrailing: with lastLogIdx equal to the snapshot index at snapshot time, 4 <= 10 and 4 <= 25, so it returns without deleting; only TrailingLogs=0 lets the deletion reach the snapshot index. This corrects a reading that the earlier control might suggest - that any nonzero trailing value merely delays the loop - and it narrows the precondition of the asserted finding: the boundary is compacted away only when the snapshot index lags the log end by at least TrailingLogs at the moment of the snapshot, which TrailingLogs=0 guarantees but a default-configured quiet cluster does not. It does not weaken either asserted result, since both are scoped to their executed bases (the single-peer witness and the sealed-partition witness both ran with TrailingLogs=0), but it does mean the practical trigger is a snapshot taken while the log end is at least TrailingLogs ahead of the applied index - for example a user-triggered snapshot during a write backlog - rather than a routine periodic snapshot in a caught-up cluster.
counterevidence: Both nonzero-TrailingLogs cases converged with zero snapshot installs and the peer reaching the leader's applied index, so compaction reaching the snapshot boundary is necessary for the loop and not merely incidental.
In the nonzero cases the applied index at snapshot time equalled the log end, so the earlier control's convergence (TrailingLogs=3) and these are the same effect, not two separate protections.
limitations: Source-only in this batch: the three-case harness has not been executed by the controller, and the quoted numbers are non-retained local runs.
Only three (trailing, post) combinations were sampled; the intermediate threshold was not bisected.

The harness takes snapshots only through the user API at a quiet moment; a threshold-triggered snapshot during a backlog was not executed, and that is the configuration the narrowed precondition points at.
Same in-process five-node setup as before: InmemTransport/InmemStore, equal 1 s timeouts.

scope.description: Same sealed-partition five-node history as the previous control, executed for three (TrailingLogs, post-snapshot entries) cases: (0,0), (10,20) and (25,20). Each case isolates {leader, partner} from the other three peers in both directions, lets the leader replicate uncommitted commands to the partner, has the majority elect a successor that snapshots at index 4, optionally commits further entries past that snapshot, then heals and observes the partner's InstallSnapshot count and indexes plus each node's store bounds.
assumptions: Applying entries after the snapshot but before the heal models a leader whose log end is ahead of its snapshot index at snapshot time, which is the quantity compactLogsWithTrailing consumes.
The partner's FSM Restore count identifies InstallSnapshot installs without touching production logic.
Precondition guards skip rather than fail so a timing miss yields no observation.
excluded: No threshold-triggered snapshot under a live write backlog; snapshots are user-triggered at a quiet point.
No network transport and no bisection of the (trailing, post) boundary.

experiment.prefix: For each (trailing, post): MakeClusterCustom(Peers=5, Bootstrap=true, Conf{TrailingLogs: trailing, SnapshotInterval:1h, SnapshotThreshold:1<<20, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout:1s, CommitTimeout:10ms}, MakeFSMFunc returning a Restore-counting MockFSM). Wait for a leader; partner=followers[0], others=remaining three; disconnect leader<->other and partner<->other in both directions and emit partition; base=leader.LastIndex(); fire five leader.Apply calls; wait until partner.LastIndex()>base and emit divergent_prefix with trailing_logs; wait for a successor among others, apply one command, Snapshot(), emit successor_snapshot with the successor's store bounds; apply `post` further commands and emit post_snapshot_applies with the successor's last index and store bounds; FullyConnect(); emit the per-node timeline at 0/200/400/700/1000/1300 ms including the partner's Restore count; finally emit rejoin_observe with the restore counts, both peers' indexes, both store bounds and trailing_logs.
experiment.responsibility: The audit must state the precondition of a progress failure in terms of the parameters a deployment actually sets, not in terms of a chosen harness value.
